clue.text: Young rustic may have his own share one day?

definitions.text: Young rustic may have his own share one day?

parts.words: Young rustic may have his own share one day?
parts.note: a lad working the fields hopes one day to own the blade of the plough, its share, punning on a share as a stake in property

explanation.surface: A farm lad dreams of inheriting a stake in the family land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'share' reads as a portion of property, but a ploughshare is the cutting blade of a plough; the lad who walks behind one may one day own his own.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm lad who guides the plough horses is a young country worker.

clue.text: Basin for a studious reader outside the circle

indicators.note: the reader's letters are placed around the circle's letters, sitting outside them

parts.note: one who pores over books is a porer
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A bookworm sits at a washbasin beyond some circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A porringer is a small bowl for porridge or soup, a kind of basin.

clue.text: No area for an oxidizing agent

parts.note: no as a figure is nought, the round letter O
a zone is an area

explanation.surface: A region is declared free of any chemical oxidant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone, a form of oxygen with three atoms, is a powerful oxidant used in bleaching and water treatment.

clue.text: Secures assistance? It's denied

parts.note: to secure something is to gain it, so secures gives gains
aid is assistance

explanation.surface: Someone obtains help, only to have it refused.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or deny, so its past form means denied.

clue.text: Residence for a Parisian lass in E3?

indicators.note: the French article and the girl are placed inside the district's name

parts.note: E3 is the London postcode of Bow, in the East End
a Parisian would say un for the article a
a gal is a lass

explanation.surface: Where might a French girl live in London's East End?
explanation.walkthrough: E3 is the London postcode district of Bow in the East End: the clue asks for its name, not the code.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a one-storey house, a type of dwelling.

clue.text: River plant

definitions.meaning: a Scottish river, celebrated in Border ballads
..., or milfoil, is a feathery wild flower

explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow Water flows through the Scottish Borders, and yarrow is also a common white-flowered herb.

clue.text: Peter (Potter) tailed by Levantine law man

indicators.note: to tail something is to cut off its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Peter Rabbit is Beatrix Potter's character

explanation.surface: Beatrix Potter's Peter is followed by a lawyer from the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailed by' reads as followed by, but here 'tailed' means docked of its tail, and 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish teacher of religious law, the scholar of Torah, is a law man of the Levant.

clue.text: Broadcasts some army songs

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, RE, are part of the British Army
lays are songs or ballads

explanation.surface: A radio station plays some military tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: To relay a programme is to transmit it, so relays are broadcasts.

clue.text: Unusual start of the hotel bar engagement

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters appear in an unexpected order
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An odd beginning to a romance in a hotel bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes T from 'the'; 'Unusual' rearranges T with HOTEL and BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothal is a formal promise to marry, an engagement.

clue.text: Flower, in Hindustani

indicators.note: in tells us the answer is tucked inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A blossom named in the Hindustani language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword trick: a river is something that flows. The Indus is a great river of the subcontinent.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a thing that flows, and the Indus is a major South Asian river.

clue.text: But not an oxford scholar this islander

definitions.text: But not an oxford scholar this islander

parts.words: But not an oxford scholar this islander
parts.note: a Rhodes scholar studies at Oxford; this person shares the name but is simply a native of the Greek island

explanation.surface: This islander, the clue insists, is no Oxford academic.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhodes scholarships send students to Oxford, so the name sounds academic; here it is just a native of the Greek island of Rhodes.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Rhodes, the Greek island in the Aegean, is so called.

clue.text: Told of account returned, overdrawn

indicators.note: of here means made out of, the turned story forming the core of the red letters

parts.note: an overdrawn account is in the red

indicators.note: returned means the story's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a tale is an account

explanation.surface: Someone is informed that a statement came back showing an overdraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns TALE into ELAT, which sits inside RED; 'of' is a loose container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell it, so related means told.

clue.text: Thoughts for an article written in mid-March?

indicators.note: the article is inserted into the date's letters

parts.note: the Ides of March fall on the fifteenth, in the middle of the month
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Notions for a piece composed in the middle of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' suggests a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical article A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas are notions or concepts formed in the mind.

clue.text: Unknown writer, shortly to be just that

definitions.text: Unknown writer, shortly to be just that

parts.words: Unknown writer, shortly to be just that
parts.note: the shortened label for an author of unknown name is Anon, and the full word is that very description

explanation.surface: An obscure author is about to remain unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' reads as soon, but means in short: the abbreviation ANON. is written under works by an unknown author.
explanation.definitionFit: Of unknown or unnamed authorship, as a nameless writer is.

clue.text: Ointment container used by a sea-cook, say ?

indicators.note: say tells us to go by how the phrase sounds when spoken

parts.note: a ship's cook works in the galley, so a pot used there is a galley pot

explanation.surface: A ship's cook keeps balm in one of his kitchen pots.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship's kitchen is its galley; a galley pot sounds like this small earthenware jar.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallipot is a small glazed pot used by apothecaries to hold medicines and salves.

clue.text: Jacobson adopts non-Asian creed — that's monstrous!

parts.note: Levi was one of the sons of Jacob in Genesis

indicators.note: non- tells us the letters of the word Asian are removed from the creed

parts.note: the Athanasian Creed is a Christian statement of faith

explanation.surface: A man named Jacobson embraces a creed without Asia, to outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jacobson' looks like a surname; it is a son of Jacob, LEVI. 'non-Asian' strips ASIAN from ATHANASIAN, leaving ATHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leviathan is a huge sea monster of the Bible, so it is something monstrous.

clue.text: Cleaner type of fish

definitions.meaning: a trout-like fish of cold lakes

explanation.definitionFit: A char, short for charwoman, does cleaning; the char is also a salmon-family freshwater fish.

clue.text: Repository for one's liquid assets

parts.note: liquid assets usually means ready money, but here it is literal water, stored in a large artificial lake

explanation.surface: A bank vault where one keeps cash to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid assets' is financial jargon for cash; read literally it is water, kept in an artificial lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a store of water, a repository for something liquid.

clue.text: A gentle' touch confines loose ends, like Herrick's shoe-string

indicators.note: the stroke surrounds the picked letters, confining them

parts.note: a caress is a gentle touch

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A soft stroke holds stray ends together, like a poet's shoelace.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Herrick's poem 'Delight in Disorder' praises 'a careless shoe-string'. 'ends' takes L and E from 'loose'.
explanation.definitionFit: Herrick's poem admires a shoelace tied in a casual, negligent way.

clue.text: Message about superior record of criminal

indicators.note: the message's letters go around the others

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, a message
U is the abbreviation for upper class, superior
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A telegram about an outstanding record of a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminal conduct is blameworthy, deserving guilt.

clue.text: Doctor leaves club, causing split

indicators.note: leaves means the doctor departs from the club word

parts.note: a driver is a golf club

explanation.surface: A doctor quits his club, causing a rift.
explanation.walkthrough: D and R leave from opposite ends of DRIVER, leaving the inner letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To rive is an old word for tearing or cleaving apart.

clue.text: About Cicero dropping one poet

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: dropping means one letter is left out of the orator's name

parts.note: Marcus Tullius Cicero, the Roman orator
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something about Cicero letting a single matter fall makes a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Cicero's full name was Marcus Tullius Cicero; removing I from TULLIUS leaves TULLUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Catullus was a Roman lyric writer, a contemporary of Cicero.

clue.text: It got mixed with the Snark hunter's bowsprit

definitions.text: It got mixed with the Snark hunter's bowsprit

parts.words: It got mixed with the Snark hunter's bowsprit
parts.note: in Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark, the ship's bowsprit got mixed up with the steering gear at the stern

explanation.surface: Something got muddled with the bowsprit on the Snark hunters' ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll writes that the Bellman's ship's bowsprit 'got mixed with the rudder sometimes'.
explanation.definitionFit: The steering blade at the stern of a ship, which Carroll's crew confused with the spar at the bow.

clue.text: West End lake border?

definitions.meaning: a famous street in London's West End

explanation.definitionFit: The Strand is a London street running through the West End; a strand is also the shore of a lake or sea.

clue.text: Not a great work of art, seen from all angles?

definitions.text: Not a great work of art, seen from all angles?

parts.words: Not a great work of art, seen from all angles?
parts.note: a small piece of sculpture is not great in size, and being three-dimensional can be viewed from every side

explanation.surface: A minor artwork that has been examined from every perspective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great' reads as masterly but means large; a sculpture in the round is seen from all sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A small carved or cast figure is a little sculpture, viewable from all round.

clue.text: Cook as certain vessels move

definitions.meaning: to cook food over boiling water
ships powered by boilers are driven by water vapour

explanation.definitionFit: Steaming is a cooking method using vapour, and steamships are said to steam along.

clue.text: Model question, of some difficulty.

definitions.meaning: an artist's model is one who poses

explanation.definitionFit: One who poses for a painter is a model; a puzzling problem is also called this.

clue.text: Just one of Iago's drowsy medicines

definitions.text: Just one of Iago's drowsy medicines

parts.words: Just one of Iago's drowsy medicines
parts.note: in Othello, Iago speaks of poppy, mandragora and all the drowsy medicines of the world, naming them in the plural

explanation.surface: A single sleeping draught from Iago's list.
explanation.walkthrough: Iago says 'Not poppy, nor mandragora, Nor all the drowsy syrups of the world' can restore Othello's sleep; the clue asks for the singular.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet medicinal liquid, one of the sleep-inducing draughts Iago mentions.

clue.text: Rough hide can disguise an ant-eater

indicators.note: to disguise the words is to change their appearance by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A coarse skin can hide a spiny animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' is part of the surface picture; 'disguise' rearranges HIDE and CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna, or spiny anteater, is an Australian egg-laying mammal that feeds on ants.

clue.text: It stops one harbouring mates, among others

definitions.text: It stops one harbouring mates, among others

parts.words: It stops one harbouring mates, among others
parts.note: a government order keeps ships in port, so a vessel with its mates and the rest of the crew stays in harbour

explanation.surface: Something prevents a person hiding friends, along with other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbouring' reads as sheltering, but the order detains ships, with their mates among the crew, in harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban on shipping or trade, holding vessels in port.

clue.text: Island alternative to a feudal lordship

parts.note: the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: An island as a substitute for a feudal estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor was the estate and jurisdiction held by a lord under the feudal system.

clue.text: Boxer's complaint, possibly, may go to the wall

definitions.meaning: a boxer is a breed of dog, and dogs catch a viral disease
a kind of paint applied to walls

explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is a canine viral disease and also a water-based paint for walls.
